To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the acidic tumor microenvironment is a major cause of tumor resistance to chemotherapy; (2) proton pump inhibitors (a class of drugs used for gastric acid control) can inhibit cancer growth and metastasis; (3) cancer cells use a fermentation pathway for energy production; and (4) cancer cells use EVs to communicate with their microenvironment and to promote metastasis.
tumor acidity, proton pumps, fermentation, and extracellular vehicles (micro and nanosized) are the common features that can be targeted to fight against cancer.

The main takeaway from our work is that
cancer is a disease of the microenvironment, and the main targets are the tumor microenvironment itself and the mechanisms that allow tumor cells to live and grow in the hostile environment.
cancer is not a disease but a state of our body, and that we need to find a way of living with it.

cancer is an infectious disease and the magic bullet against it should be a drug against infection, rather than a drug against cancer.
